p0perf-202609: Short version: all 18 rows of the extraction are supported by the raw files, and every TPS, TTFT, n, and sd value matched a recomputation from the underlying logs. No row was dropped and none was missing. The corrections below are to descriptive fields (placement wording, source-file citations, timestamps), not to any number.

Words used here: runtron = tron's command-line tool; CI harness = the nightly systems_test throughput test (testlib/tps.py through exec/more-testing-r1/st_perf.py) driving a rinzler server; TPS = decode tokens per second per user; TTFT = time to first token; kill switch = TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1; engine = one rinzler process; sd = sample standard deviation (statistics.stdev).

What was recomputed (read-only; nothing run or edited):
- runtron, 48 logs (2 days x 4 cells x 6 reps): per-rep TPS = mean of the 8 'average tok/s' lines, per-rep TTFT = max of the 8 'Parsing the prompt took' lines. Every per-rep value equals summary.json to full precision. Means and sample sd over the kept reps equal summary.json (sd is statistics.stdev, n-1, per summarize.py mean_sd). The 0911 tp2 off rep2 EARLY-STOP (73 vs 253 tokens) is real; excluding it gives n=5.
- CI harness, 26 cells (8 on 0911, 18 on 0913): perf.json tps_mean and ttft_mean_ms (pooled perf.json on 0913) equal summary.json; recomputing from the 'Done (TTFT=..., X TPS)' lines of perf.log / perf-e*.log reproduces them to within 0.001 TPS and 0.5 ms (the harness rounds ttft_mean_ms to an integer). Means and sd over reps equal summary.json.
- Arm labels checked against meta.json env and the rinzler logs: off and on show 'HW attention disabled ... USE_HW_ATTN=0'; fpga shows 'HW attention enabled ... engagement=127'. Every log shows the expected Version/hash (47f6f2dc on 0911, 544ca05c on 0913) and instance/App CPU list.
- Nightly reference numbers (185.38 TPS / 507 ms tp2; 147.21 / 635 tp4) confirmed in ci-run-34559196745.log lines 2130 and 2291 (the extractor had not re-derived them).
